title: model-specific-runtime: GQA/MQA tuning + kernel selection for Llama/Mistral/Qwen
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: We observed model-specific performance and correctness quirks for Llama, Mistral and Qwen families when using GQA/MQA quantized variants under the runtime's kernel selection and batching heuristics. These issues manifested as throughput regressions on long sequences, occasional KV-cache misalignment for GQA int4 backends, and suboptimal kernel choices for Mistral attention shapes. This PR introduces model-specific tuning hooks into the kernel selector, fixes a KV cache offset bug for GQA packed state, and adds MQA-aware continuous batching heuristics. Summary of changes: 1) kernel_selector: add model profile table and runtime scoring that prefers fused-attention kernels for Mistral at seq_len >= 1024, and prefers Qwen's split-FFN kernels for medium-length contexts to reduce memory traffic. 2) kv_cache: fix offset computation when loading packed GQA cache entries that could cause token misalignment under certain concat-and-stream patterns; add regression test. 3) continuous_batcher: add MQA-aware batch packing policy that avoids cross-quant variant packing when quant tables differ; introduces a per-request quant_id tag propagated through scheduler. 4) models/*: model-specific small kernels and landing tests for Llama alignment, Mistral fused kernels, Qwen split-FFN micro-optimizations. 5) benchmarks/perf-canary/gqa_mqa_suite.yml: new benchmark harness to measure GQA/MQA latency and throughput across seq len buckets. Results: on internal perf-canary for c6g-gpu nodes: - Mistral: 18-23% median p99 latency improvement for 1024+ sequences due to fused-attention selection. - Qwen: 22% throughput improvement for 512-1024 contexts by switching to split-FFN kernel and reducing memory copies. - GQA: resolved observed token misalignment bug; end-to-end e2e test coverage included. Compatibility and safety: changes are behind model-profile opt-in flags; default behavior unchanged unless model profile is present or a per-deployment opt-in is enabled. Rollout plan: gate behind feature flag runtime.enable_model_profiles=false by default; staged rollout to Dedicated canaries and then Hosted subset. Testing: unit tests for kv cache offsets, integration tests with streaming enabled, perf-canary runs attached. Notes: this also removes a fragile fallback that forced non-fused kernels on all Mistral variants (was causing regressions for newer kernels). Related: ENG-1723 (runtime kernel selection work), SUP-4982 (support ticket describing token misalignment).

diff_snippets:
runtime/kv_cache.rs @@ fn compute_packed_offset(packed_idx: usize) { - let base = packed_idx * ENTRY_SIZE; + // if GQA packed layout, entries are stored with header per 32-token block
+ let base = packed_idx * ENTRY_SIZE + match layout { Layout::GqaPacked => header_size(packed_idx), _ => 0 };

scheduler/continuous_batcher.rs @@ fn try_pack(batch, req) { - if req.quant == batch.quant { pack(req) } else { fallback(); } + // MQA: do not pack across differing quant tables; use quant_id tags to allow safe packing
+ if req.quant_id.is_some() && batch.quant_id == req.quant_id { pack(req) } else if batch.quant_id.is_none() && req.quant_id.is_none() { pack(req) } else { mark_separate_queue(req) } }

release_notes: Model-specific runtime optimizations: fixes token misalignment for GQA packed cache, improved Mistral fused-attention kernel selection (p99 latency reduction on long context), Qwen split-FFN throughput gains for medium contexts, and MQA-aware batching policy. Backwards-compatible opt-in via runtime.enable_model_profiles flag.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: stage 1 - Dedicated canaries; stage 2 - Hosted small tenant subset; stage 3 - general rollout after 2 weeks of perf monitoring. Disable via runtime.enable_model_profiles=false if any regression.
changelog_entry: runtime: add model profile scoring for kernel selection; GQA kv_cache fix; MQA-aware batching (opt-in)
additional_context: This PR replaces an earlier coarse-grained fallback that caused fused kernels to be disabled for newer Mistral releases. Keeping behavior opt-in ensures we can roll back quickly in Hosted while allowing Dedicated customers to test. Performance numbers are from controlled perf-canary runs; production rollout requires monitoring of per-model token error rates and latency SLOs.
